references.text: Peter immediately asks if he can follow Jesus now, and Jesus confirms that he must follow later, which leads directly to the prophecy that he will deny Jesus three times before following him.

Jesus later explains to Peter that when he is old he will stretch out his hands and be taken where he does not want to go, and then Jesus gives him the direct call: "Follow me", as the fulfillment of the promise to follow later.

Jesus confirms that he is going away to prepare a place for them, and that he will come again and take the disciples to himself, so that they may be where he is, which is the goal of following him later.
Jesus prays that those whom he has received may be with him where he is, to see his glory, which is the ultimate fulfillment of following him wherever he goes.
Jesus calls everyone to take up their cross and follow him, a call that Peter could not fulfill immediately, but which he was later called to live out.

Jesus asks James and John if they can drink the cup he is about to drink, and they answer yes, but Jesus confirms that they will indeed drink it, even though they do not know exactly how, paralleling the fact that Peter could not follow now but would later.
